subject: TeleMed - conditional processing & TIA scoping clarification
messages:
From: Dr. Priyanka Rao <priya@telemed.ai>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@telemed.ai>, legal@telemed.ai
Date: 2026-03-30T08:12:00Z
Subject: Questions on DPA + TIA scoping for UK clinical pilot

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we scope the pilot we need to confirm a few items for our legal and security teams before we proceed with a DPA signature and the UK Addendum. I've attached a short list (telemed_questions_030926.pdf). High-level asks:

- Can Redwood accept UK Addendum / IDTA with standard TIA sequencing (we may need an explicit clause about onshore processing for a subset of records)?
- Who is the exporter/importer in your model when requests route through Dedicated vs Hosted?
- Subprocessor custody: we need a clear map of any subprocessors that have access to unredacted clinical text and whether KMS keys are customer-managed or Redwood-managed.
- Retention & deletion: our retention policy for pilot data is 60 days; can you confirm deletion and log evidence?

We are trying to avoid protracted back-and-forth. If you can send proposed language or a short technical note that addresses these items, that would help our legal ops. Is it possible to get a draft UK Addendum with track changes?

Cheers,
Priyanka
Dr. Priyanka Rao
Head of Programs, TeleMed Health

--- Attachment: telemed_questions_030926.pdf (3 pages, questionnaire)
From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
To: Dr. Priyanka Rao <priya@telemed.ai>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-03-31T14:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA + TIA scoping for UK clinical pilot

Hi Priyanka —

Appreciate the clear list. Short answers up front, then next steps below:

1) UK Addendum / IDTA + TIA sequencing: Yes — Redwood can sign the UK Addendum. For the pilot we typically include a scoped TIA (DTIA) that documents which subprocessors and processing locations are in-scope. We can include an explicit onshore-processing exception for the small subset you flagged; we usually implement that as a routing policy + contractual routing guarantee.

2) Exporter/importer model: For Hosted API mode, Redwood (controller/processor relationship per DPA) is the exporter and remote cloud regions may act as subprocessors/importers depending on the destination. For Dedicated deployments where the customer pins region and keys, the customer is effectively controlling import activities — we'll reflect this distinction in the DPA wording.

3) Subprocessor custody & KMS: We run a short subprocessor matrix and will provide explicit flags for any subprocessors that touch unredacted clinical text. By default our platform uses Redwood-managed KMS; we offer customer-managed KMS for Dedicated and Private deployments (HSM integrations available). We'll attach the current matrix and a proposed clause for key custody.

4) Retention & deletion: We can support 60-day retention for pilot data and provide deletion confirmation logs + audit timestamps. We'll need to map retention events to your expected retention triggers (session end vs ingestion).

Next steps: I've attached a working UK Addendum draft (uk_addendum_draft_v2.docx) and our current subprocessor matrix (subprocessor_matrix_v3.csv). Kimberly and Grace are looped in for technical and legal confirmation. Can we target a redline back by Friday, 2026-04-02? If helpful, we can do a 30-minute call to walk the matrix.

Thanks —
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

--- Attachments: uk_addendum_draft_v2.docx, subprocessor_matrix_v3.csv

Date: 2026-04-01T09:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA + TIA scoping for UK clinical pilot

On Mon, Mar 31, 2026 at 14:05 Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Jonas: short answers up front...

Adding technical detail from infra/security so TeleMed has clear evidence for the TIA:

- Subprocessors that can access unredacted text: currently our tokenizer/ingest service (Redwood Ingest) and our retriever/cache tier may hold plaintext briefly for real-time features. Both run on contracted cloud instances; neither is in a separate legal entity. We'll mark both as in-scope for the DTIA.

- KMS model: for Hosted we use Redwood-managed keys (AWS KMS customer master keys in our account). For Dedicated we can enable BYOK via AWS KMS grants or a customer HSM integration (we have an HSM onboarding playbook). The UK Addendum draft includes optional clauses for BYOK and a short template for KMS proof (envelope encryption metadata + CMK ARNs).

- Key custody evidence: we can provide (a) CMK ARNs + grants audit, (b) rotation schedule and last-rotation timestamp, (c) limited access IAM role list. These will be provided as redacted evidence packers in the DTIA.

- Deletion proof: our deletion job emits an audit line (job id, affected object ids, timestamp, sha256 of archive if persisted briefly) and we can produce a signed log extract for your legal team. For 60-day retention we will chain deletion to a scheduled job and produce a signed attestation.

Open items where we need TeleMed input:
- Confirm whether onshore-processing exception requires physical UK-only compute for the subset, or whether an encryption-and-BYOK approach suffices. The former triggers Dedicated/Private recommendations.
- Any additional subprocessors (analytics partners) that TeleMed expects to be in-scope.

I'll prepare a short one-page technical note to go with the UK Addendum redline.

Kimberly Park
Director, Infrastructure Security | Redwood Inference
